Class LessonListTestingAutomation

java.lang.Object
testingAutomation.LessonListTestingAutomation
public class LessonListTestingAutomation extends Object

Title: LessonListTestingAutomation Class.

Description: A semi-automated test driver, in the style of the team's InputValidationTestingAutomation and LessonTestingAutomation classes, for the LessonsLearnedList class: the persistent list of all lessons, the my-lessons subset each contributor sees, Create, Update, and Delete through the list, keyword search, and the lock and curator-edited state the My Lessons page shows as tags.

Each test is its own method, so each has its own Javadoc stating the requirement it tests, how the code checks it, and how to read its output. Every requirement has at least two tests, at least one positive (valid use succeeds) and one negative (invalid use is refused or handled safely).

Requirements tested (from the Contributor user stories and the TP2 assignment):

  • LIST-1: There is a persistent list of all lessons learned in the system.
  • LIST-2: A contributor's list holds only the lessons that contributor added, including any a curator has edited (Contributor stories 2 and 4).
  • LIST-3: A list may be empty or arbitrarily large, and its contents are protected.
  • LIST-4: A lesson added through the list is stored in the database and the list; an invalid one is stored in neither.
  • LIST-5: A lesson updated through the list is changed in both; a refused update changes neither.
  • LIST-6: A lesson deleted through the list after confirmation is removed from both; a cancelled or refused delete changes neither.
  • LIST-7: A keyword search returns the subset of lessons that contain every keyword.
  • LIST-8: The list reports each lesson's lock and curator-edited state (for the tags).
  • LIST-9: Changes made through the list persist after the application restarts.

How to read the output: each test prints a header with its ID, requirement, and whether it is positive or negative, followed by one or more checks. Each check prints the expected and observed values (or messages) and "***Success***" when they match. A test passes only if every one of its checks succeeds. The summary at the end gives the number of tests and checks that passed and failed; a correct implementation shows 0 failures.

The tests use private in-memory databases created with the Database(String dbUrl) constructor, so they never alter the production database. LT-25 and LT-26 use a temporary database file instead, because persistence can only be shown by closing and reopening.

    • testLoadAllReturnsEveryLesson

      static void testLoadAllReturnsEveryLesson() throws Exception

      Test LT-01 (LIST-1, positive): loadAll returns every stored lesson.

      How: stores 3 lessons from 2 contributors, then calls LessonsLearnedList.loadAll and checks the list holds all 3 and includes both contributors' lessons.

      Output: two checks; each shows Expected: true and Observed: true with Success.

      Throws:
      Exception - if the test database cannot be created

    • testLoadAllOnEmptyDatabase

      static void testLoadAllOnEmptyDatabase() throws Exception

      Test LT-02 (LIST-1, negative): loadAll on a database with no lessons.

      How: calls loadAll on a new, empty database and checks that the result is an empty list rather than null, so callers can always use it safely.

      Output: one check; Expected: true, Observed: true, Success.

      Throws:
      Exception - if the test database cannot be created

    • testLoadAllWithNoDatabase

      static void testLoadAllWithNoDatabase()

      Test LT-03 (LIST-1, negative): loadAll without a database.

      How: passes null as the database and checks that an empty list is returned instead of the program failing with an exception.

      Output: one check; Expected: true, Observed: true, Success.

      static void testContributorSeesOnlyOwnLessons() throws Exception

      Test LT-04 (LIST-2, positive): a contributor's list holds exactly their lessons.

      How: stores 2 lessons for jsmith and 1 for akim, loads jsmith's list with loadForContributor, and checks it holds 2 lessons, all owned by jsmith.

      Output: two checks, each Expected: true, Observed: true, Success.

      Exception - if the test database cannot be created

      static void testOtherContributorsExcluded() throws Exception

      Test LT-05 (LIST-2, negative): other contributors' lessons are never included.

      How: checks that akim's lesson is not in jsmith's list, and that a contributor who has added nothing sees no lessons at all, even though the database holds some (Contributor story 4: "I am unable to see submissions from other contributors").

      Output: two checks, each Expected: true, Observed: true, Success.

      Exception - if the test database cannot be created

      Output: two checks, each Expected: true, Observed: true, Success.

    • testLockAndEditedStateReported

      static void testLockAndEditedStateReported() throws Exception

      Test LT-24 (LIST-8, positive): the list reports locks and curator edits.

      How: locks one field of one lesson, locks a second lesson entirely, marks the second as curator-edited, reloads the list, and checks each lesson reports the right state. This is the information the My Lessons page uses for its "Locked" and "Edited by curator" tags, and the Lesson Detail page uses to make fields read-only and disable Delete.

      Output: three checks, each Expected: true, Observed: true, Success.

      Throws:
      Exception - if the test database cannot be created
